the PDV of forage-fed cattle have a significant influence on the net absorption of energy and nutrients from the diet, and the CNCPS may be used to estimate the PDV effect on nutrient net absorption when the PDV effect is quantified.

net absorption of energy and AA across the PDV increased in response to ME, but the relationship between energy intake and net AA absorption was influenced by the AA considered, with the greatest increases in net absorption occurring for those AA that are catabolized for energy production.

In summary, our research is concerned with

the quantitative description and application of the effects of forage intake on nutrient utilization by the PDVs of forage-fed cattle, which will allow more accurate prediction of nutrient availability to the productive tissues.
the quantitation of energy and nutrient absorption in the small intestine, and the application of this information to a nutritional prediction system.
the development of a nutritional prediction model to predict nutrient utilization and growth performance of beef cattle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
net absorption of energy and AA increased linearly with increasing ME intake, and that the PDV net absorbed a greater proportion of AA when ME intake increased.
the CNCPS is a useful tool to estimate the energy and AA availability of forage diets, provided the effects of PDV metabolism on AA absorption are taken into account.
net energy and nutrient absorption increased linearly with increased ME intake in forage-fed beef cattle, and that this increase could be described by a simple linear relationship with ME intake.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the net absorption of energy and AA across the PDV is a significant component of energy and nutrient availability for productive tissues and that the Cornell Net Carbohydate and Protein System model may be used in conjunction with these data to predict nutrient absorption across the PDV.
net absorption of AA by the PDV of forage-fed cattle is highly responsive to changes in ME intake.
the PDV of beef steers fed forage diets can absorb and utilize a wide range of AA, but that net PDV absorption of AA may not be predicted by the CNCPS model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PDV is a major site of AA utilization and that this is especially the case when energy intake is increased.
net absorption of AA across the PDV increases linearly with increasing energy intake.
the PDV can be a significant source of variation in nutrient availability to productive tissues in beef cattle.
